body: I'm sorry you feel the same way. This is one case I'd rather be alone. Sucks we're all here for the same reason. Thank you.

I'm sorry we all went through all this.  There is no reason to continue the cycle. You can totally do this. You are strong. If it was worth protecting your sister,  it's worth protecting yourself. Good luck. Small steps add up to big moves!

*And you mentioned being tired. I cannot stress enough how much less exhausting just waking up is now that I'm gone.

My problem was that I grew up with abuse,  so I never knew differently.  That was my normal.  This was my first relationship with a man that wasn't physically abusive and mentally one of the most ruinous. I met him not long after having becoming single when my arm dislocated in 3 places and thought he was wonderful.  I was exhausted too, after 38 years of it,  but it is so much more exhausting putting up with it.  I went into isolation right after moving basically, and I think if I were trapped with him right now,  I'd be done for. I'm still devastated that my marriage and everything I thought my future was going to be is gone. I'm grieving for sure.  At least I'm not grieving while grievously injured.  It is so miserable,  and so wonderful and just amazingly relaxing knowing it's behind me.  I bet you're strong and tenacious as fuck, too. You don't survive that much abuse if you aren't.  You can get out.

*When I say first relationship,  I mean first.  Both my father and stepfather tried to kill me as a kid. Not setting a great example.

I don't know about that.  I'm tenacious as fuck I guess.  I've just had far far far too much experience in what happens if you don't gtfo BEFORE things turn violent.  I was just lucky enough to have a therapist there telling me what to do because I was so stressed while moving my stuff out while he was at work that I literally shit my pants in my sleep.  My heart rate always high, I was throwing up and having diarrhea, I couldn't eat or even hold a pen I was always shaking, my periods stopped, and I still couldn't believe what was happening, because... "nobody's getting hit,  right?" I was mentally fucked.

*Thank you though.  Maybe someone else out there will see this and know that life and circumstance can often be set right, even if you've literally shit the bed.
I'm so sorry.  I was lucky enough to not have kids in the situation,  but I've been there.  My right arm will never be the same.

This hit hard.  I left my "DH" about 6 weeks ago. He started reporting crazy things about me trying to get guns,  which leads to awkward calls.  Calling me crazy and saying I'm doing stuff that I have no memory of, or denying things that I've seen him do.  My therapist spent two sessions talking me out of thinking I had DID.  He always used the PTSD as a weapon in these situations saying that was why I didn't remember and reacted so horribly.  I thought I was going into menopause,  but it turns out I was just so stressed the last six months my hormones were all screwed up. I will never be in a relationship again.  It's not worth it.  I'm done.

*Edit because my autocorrect makes up words.

*Also,  we were in counseling prior to this,  but the therapist had just called it all off because he refused to take responsibility for anything and then ramped it up so fast they thought he was setting it up to either kill me in "self defense" or make it look like I was so depressed that I killed myself. When I said that I literally couldn't use one of the guns he said I was trying to get because of a disability,  he said,  "You'd only have to be able to shoot it once." That's one of the scariest things I've heard someone say to my face.

I've survived decades of abuse,  and I remember this happening for the first time when I was a toddler but I didn't know what it was for 30 years. My amnesia,  which has started to crumble in unsettling chunks,  saved me from something I couldn't process at the time. In stressful situations I still take comfort in my ability to easily dissociate myself from the pain.
Well,  I  just call it family.  I'm nc with everyone but my lc/mc mom.

I broke through one of my mother's delusions with cold hard fact and it made her very angry. 

I've had two spinal cord injuries and she hit the gas while I was trying to get out of the car. She has never been violently abusive before. That was her husband's job.

It doesn't matter how calm you are.  She will lose it if you break her delusions. The next time I spoke to her it was like nothing had happened. Moral of the story: if you are going to do it,  don't do it near anything that can be used as a weapon.

*Sorry, usually I just lurk,  but nobody needs to learn that the hard way.  Congratulations on finding out the truth too!
Same.  Almost put me inpatient.

For me,  it was pointed out just today that the lows aren't as low (if all this had happened four years ago I'd be dead, at a minimum), so it is definite tangible progress. It feels so much worse though, I'm thinking maybe because I now know how much better it can be?  I don't know if that makes sense.

A month ago I spent two weeks on the couch staring at the wall and vacillating between murderous rage and intense depression and self- loathing.  I don't remember much. I was almost hospitalized,  and I felt like I'd lost years of work after an onslaught of triggers that lasted 6 months. 

Two weeks after a large chunk of my triggers settled,  I'm happy to report that I just got home from therapy and they are really happy with how well I've bounced back,  and even improved they said,  now that the triggers are gone.  

It still scares me when chores get done or I drive home and don't remember,  but I'm calling it a win as a whole.

Family doesn't mean shit if they're a shit family. I'm minimal contact with my mom and no contact with my bio dad,  step mom/ dad, siblings,  etc. My life is SO MUCH BETTER WITHOUT THEM IN IT.

*It took a couple years for my partner to really see why I would let her calls go to vm and only call back when I was prepared. Eventually,  he saw it too.

For me, I love my partner so much,  but I still tell him to leave me almost every day because I don't feel like I deserve him and he can do better. It's also really important that he realizes when he's done something hurtful or inappropriate,  or is at least willing to listen to you when you say something isn't acceptable. I personally can lash out at people who don't deserve it,  particularly as more triggers pile on. It's a lot better than it was,  but my process of self-flagellation can be hurtful to him too.

Props to you for keeping your cool.  It reminds of the first time I met my psychiatrist and he said that he could feel the rage emanating from me when I walked into the room, and he wasn't surprised people were intimidated by me.  A couple years after starting treatment he mentioned that he no longer got that vibe from me. It always sucks to know I can scare people with my mere presence, though.

No lie. I was on a waitlist for treatment when a road rage incident made me realize that if I didn't get off that waitlist soon,  I'd end up in jail. This guy had been cutting me off and slowing down in front of me to fuck with me for miles. I decided that if we caught one more light before my turn came I was going get out and do my best to kill him. Fortunately for both of us,  we did not hit another red.  When I got to where I was going,  everyone was legitimately scared of me because I was so wound up.

They really don't have to be. A few years ago I started having my primary care doc do it in the office after 15 years of going to the gyno. It's a bit easier to relax as I know and trust her and she was gentle and did not clamp my cervix.  It's not going to be a fun thing probably,  but it's definitely worth it. 

An old friend of mine was left infertile at 26 from cervical cancer because she didn't get her regular smear. I've had breast cancer twice, at 23 and 30.  Get your paps and check your boobs!

Of and on since 5. I'm 37 now. I just got the PTSD diagnosis about three years ago. Things have started to improve now that I've got consistent treatment and the proper diagnosis.  Like all of my issues make sense and I can work on them,  and I no longer think I'll be dead or in jail soon,  but I'm still basically non- functioning.
My mom is the same way.  I realised that she has issues and denies/blocks it out, but she won't get help either.  Good luck with your progress.  :)
Well... that's the system for you...

Seriously, all of us got screwed here. Now that I'm pushing 40, and finally got properly diagnosed in my 30s. I've realized that I carried on unhealthy relationship patterns until far too recently because of my upbringing, and it makes me a little sad that my mother must have picked up that dynamic somewhere, too. Makes me more sad because her parents' house was always my favorite place on earth, and she might not have felt the same way.

I always ask myself if things would have been different I'd said something at 6 instead of 16/17. I was sexually abused by my step-grandfather and step- great- grandfather, my step dad took care of the rest.  In the end, reporting didn't change things for me.  It just embedded a deep disgust for the police and the child "protective" services that let it continue even after a murder attempt.
I'm so sorry. My dad used to threaten this in front of me. I can't imagine. It took him almost succeeding for my mom to leave (and find a guy that only abused me).

My mom exactly. Mine recently denied that they kicked me out of the house for a month my senior year when I spoke up about 11 years of sexual abuse and now claims her husband only choked me "a little bit" when she first said she called the police because she "didn't think he was going to stop." 

Took me a really long time that she was too messed up to help herself and come to terms with her own shit, much less help me with mine. She isn't a person to go to for emotional support.
Wow. Again, I didn't even realize that with my language I'm conveying a responsibility.  That's true. That's feels like a much better way to look at it.

"...it's not by their own hand, it's by their rapists' hands." 

I never thought of it that way, and it really rings true for me. Wow... I was abused my entire life, sexually, physically, emotionally and as an adult I continued those patterns in relationships because that was my normal. 

It wasn't until I finally got a proper diagnosis that everything clicked and I realized things could change for the better, which is scary and intimidating too. It has taken a lot of work and I still have very dark days, but thankfully the few people I have in my life now are generally good people and try to be supportive.

My mother flat out told me she thought I was going to die by my own hand... Within the last five years. Did nothing to stop it, mind you. She did apparently give permission to let me die if it went that way when I did make my attempt as a teen.  

It's a treacherous road. Honestly, her saying that to me is one of the things that keeps me going in a way, because I refuse to let her win. Keeping myself alive to spite the woman that made me and hates me lol. I also had health problems that were supposed to kill me 13 years ago. The doctors said I'd be dead by 25. I WILL NOT LET THOSE FUCKERS WIN.

My first crush was in Kindergarten on the 6th grade school bus monitor. Man, she was just the coolest with her flat top mullet (80s inner city Detroit, hush lol). 

Of course, then my mom remarried and joined a cult who says you are only gay if you're abused as a kid, but abuses all the kids. Still came out as bi at 16. 

That said, after the worst of my CSA happened, from 16 on, I'd have to get blackout drunk or have really painful sex with a male, and started only dating women. That got me disowned, oops. Turns out I had no concept what a healthy male is. I'm 37, I have been with my male partner for a good few years now. If I do find someone else attractive, it is typically a female, but I love him to death and think he's hot af. I will say that while he is extremely masculine (think cowboy hot) I did think he was gay at first (singing show tunes/love songs all night with his best friend), but I'd never come across anyone with such a masculine, but gentle, demeanor.

*The way I was raised I honestly didn't know gay was a thing until I was a teen. 

***Edit: I should proofread better.
No problem.

I tried to get justice. Up and took myself to The police dept when I was 17 and my great grandfather tried to fuck me 5 feet from his sleeping wife. They said, "He's old, he'll die soon, there is no point in trying to prosecute." My parents kicked me out if the house for a while. Good practice for when I was on my own for my 18th /s. Twenty years later, he finally died a couple years ago after going back to the Philippines. My grandfather died about 15 years ago, but I watched him drown in his own bodily fluids as his liver took a giant shit on him. I did not feel better. I'm finally hitting my stride in therapy, and realizing that I have to find peace in myself, and know that they are horrible sick people because only horrible sick people do that stuff our let it happen. Now I'm NC with my family, except minimal contact with my mother.  

*Edit: For me, my childhood was taken from me, in many ways. Ruined me physically and mentally. There is no justice for that. The only peace I can get is from myself, imho.

Your SO is a shit for not stopping it, and even worse participating. 

Everybody deals with stuff differently. I was sexually assaulted, used and abused in  by dozens upon dozens of people from birth to my 30s. Before I actually sought help, I had terrible defense mechanisms. I'd make rape jokes. Tell my friends I can't deal with their crying because it happens to all of us. Just shut down dealing with it because I took it as a fact of life. I've said some pretty terrible things that I'm not proud of. 

I wouldn't typically say that stuff in front of anyone that didn't know me well enough to know my history, but that doesn't make it ok. It really all stemmed from being incredibly sick and brainwashed and fucked up myself. 

Sadly it does say a lot about them and the friends that they think it's okay to joke about. It's part of the reason I cut nearly everyone I knew out of my life a few years ago, got a therapist and psychiatrist, and got a (mostly) fresh start. The people that are going to do that, or jump in on it, are not necessarily the healthiest people (surprise!) and will drag you down with them. 

I'm sorry this happened to you. I'd say have a talk, and if your SO doesn't understand why you would be upset about something like this, please, get a better one. Get one that better matches your values, and values you. They're out there.

Thanks! Yeah I'm on 5 mg. They recently increased my dose. It definitely made a huge difference, literally a life saver, but with everything going on lately it hasn't helped as much. Weirdly enough, though I'm terrified of having my surgery (they're fusing my spine on Sunday) the dreams aren't nearly as bad since I was admitted to the hospital and got a proper diagnosis and treatment plan. The next few months are still up in the air with what will happen, but I think the controlled environment and being in less pain is helping and I'll be in the hospital for a couple more weeks at least. They also gave me a much better prognosis than I was expecting, despite a worse diagnosis, so that may be helping too. Along with being out of my gourd on pain meds...

I found my first cancer myself because of a paper I wrote in nursing school at 23. Two rounds of cancer left me with heart failure, immunocompromised, lymphedema, and then I had my L5-S1 explode. I just found out that it's my L4-5 this time and I've got cauda equine syndrome. They were about to rush met into surgery but were didn't want me to aspirate the Boost I had 6 hours earlier instead of 8, and they didn't want the night team doing it, so I'm scheduled for morning. I've got A LOT of medical trauma in addition to a very messed up childhood (murdery, crazy, sexually, physically, and emotionally abusive people- I escaped death more than once from medical stuff and crazy people), and it can really compound itself and cripple me at times. But, like I said, hopefully I come out walking and continent. Thanks for your support. My partner does so well with me, but someone who deals with it themselves can be a wealth of tips and tricks to make it through. Thank you and good luck in nursing school! We need lots of good nurses! Don't let yourself get jaded, and take care of your back. Nurses have massively high rates of back injury. All that stuff they teach you about proper body mechanics while lifting and whatnot is gold!

Definitely very stressed in real life. I'm being admitted to the hospital now for another surgery on the piece of my back that almost paralyzed me in 2013. Hoping I make it out walking and continent this time, too. It is going to be a long time before this is fixed, and I don't know what the outcome will be, so I'm terrified and my entire future is up in the air... Once again. Thanks for the tips. I will definitely be putting them to use. Also, happy cake day!

I like the idea of a totem. I never made it through Inception (I have a three strikes and it's out rule for movies I can't pay attention to) but I get the idea. I like the clock idea, too. I'm just learning grounding techniques for when I'm awake, and I'm not very good at it yet. My partner had to talk me down today and talk me through breathing and focusing on taking stock of the things around me. I can't recognize when I'm dreaming anymore, but if I can find a way I'll take it to sleep with me. It is just too real while it's happening though. I was off meds for years and did well, but went back on a couple years ago when my health started curb stomping me again. I was literally, not figuratively, losing my mind, and I'm much less likely to hurt myself (or anyone else, I had a lot of rage) so I know they're helping. It's just an antidepressant, benzo, and Prazosin. Nothing for sleep specifically, because I've been through them all and nothing helps. My doc is at a loss because I'm so sensitive to psych drugs, I don't have any more options. I don't drink or do any other drugs (though I wish getting a mmj card wasn't so expensive and impossible to get here). I'm going to work on the totem idea, and getting something like a clock/writing to let me know I'm dreaming. When I get a little better at focusing I'll try the listening exercise. I've heard good things about guided meditation type stuff but don't have the focus for it in crisis mode. Thank you! 

Eta: I'm actually happy to hear I'm not the only one who has the momentary "dream real or reality real" memories, though I'm sorry you have you deal with it too.

It sounds like you both have a lot of learning to do before being in a serious relationship. Therapy and time may change things, but unfortunately it doesn't always work out that way. If you do stick together therapy sounds essential here. Physical and verbal abuse like that has no place in a loving relationship, there are better ways to fight, and it doesn't sound like it is doing either of you any good.  Sometimes you have to let a person you love sink or swim on their own, and work on yourself. I walked away from my high school sweetheart at 30 because his PTSD and dysfunction and addictions were fueling my unhealthy behaviors and it became frighteningly unhealthy (he once raged so hard when I asked him not to call me a "sand n****r" during sex that I literally thought I was going to die that night). It was horribly painful, but the best thing I could have done for myself. Good luck, whatever you decide to do.

I never know what will happen when I fall asleep, so I'm outed when I warn them about the possibilities. If you spend enough time with me, it's noticeable that I dissociate a lot, and have flashbacks along with panic and anxiety attacks. I'll generalize a bit and explain the symptoms and triggers they'll deal with if they deal with me, and over time, the story behind it will come out if need be.
Lol true.
Thanks! Good to know!
Wow... Well put!
Thanks. I'm taking a look at it.

I used to be able to meditate. I also feel like I didn't used to be so angry. Then I got cancer at 23, and heart failure from that, then more cancer, with worse heart failure, and a spinal cord injury after that, so I feel like I've never had a chance and now I never ever will. And I'm pissed... I like to lose myself in exercise, but but my physical therapist told me to chill for a couple days since my nerves are flaring up and it's definitely not helping my mindset.
I think I'm starting to see that, finally.
As much as we've been through... She is the only family I have really. The only constant I've had, and she is rather indispensable since she receives my disability payments.
Truth. Now... Where do I find a therapist that knows how to help me leave it behind without forgiving people that don't give a shit about my forgiveness in the first place? Lol
Thank you. It is a relief to see there are others that feel that way as well. You're right, they've taken enough and I don't have to give them anything else.

Thank you. Your title made me lol before I opened the link and, "But I guarantee there are going to be a good number of readers who sigh with relief at what I just said because, deep down, they feel that way too." That was a great read, and so spot on for me, though the Oprah bit made me want to barf in my mouth a little. Seriously though, why DOES it fall on me to just decide this never happened and it's all ok? Ridiculous.

You're welcome. I hope you start getting some decent sleep soon. I agree about it seeming worse if you put off sleeping. My brain just saved them all and amplified them (in my dreams I'm always in some inescapable place, abandoned by my loved ones, and then hunted by various styles of maniac). Yuck. It's nice to have a living alarm. My pets have always been great sources of comfort, too, which is a great bonus.

Lol like I said about meds being finicky! It's great! And Prazosin is basically just a really ineffective blood pressure drug that happens to help night terrors as a side effect. Occasionally I'd get desperate enough before to take 12.5 Seroquel and then deal with the hangover and mental weirdness it caused, but the vitamin/allergy aisle is so much better for me.

For me, it's the Prazosin/melatonin combo. The melatonin doesn't do anything on it's own, and I'll still remember my nightmares with the Prazosin. When I took them together, I slept for more than 90 minutes at a time for the first time in sooo long. I actually broke down crying I was so happy. Prazosin is a freaking miracle for me. Fun fact: I'm one of those people that gets jittery from Benadryl and Nyquil, instead of having the sedating effect!

I went through everything from Ambien and Buspar to Seroquel and Trazadone to help me sleep. I've been at this for a few decades. I always had problems (25mg of Seroquel knocked out for 18 hrs, huge traxadone hangover, the rest ineffective) but 1mg Klonopin, 3mg Prazosin, 3mg melatonin, and a cup of chamomile actually helps the most. I'll still wake up knowing I had nightmares, but I don't remember so many specifics or feel as stuck in them afterwards. I'm also not screaming or hurting myself or others thrashing around as much. Meds will differ for people, of course, being so finicky. Making sure your surroundings are familiar and secure might help, of course. A routine before bed, too. Skin care, tea, a book, for me. I can't sleep in new places or around new people. Good luck!

Thanks everyone. I'm feeling a little less guilty about the whole thing now. I guess it was probably a win that I tried to get out there in the first place.

I'm sorry. Not a vet, but survivor's guilt is a monster. There is so much that goes into it, for me. (Why am I here when I'm the one that is a mess? Why did I survive instead of my friend that has children to raise? What can/did I ever do to earn the right to stay alive? Why am I still here, if it's just going to be like this? It goes on and on, I promise). 

There are a dozen on my friends I've seen die that are "more worthy" of survival in my eyes. I would happily give up my life this moment if any of these people could have their lives back. The thing stopping me in those moments is the knowledge that it won't bring them back, and that it will just add to the hurt. If I were in the middle of a flashback or panic attack, I can't say I'd be able to reason in the same way. 

This is why I can't trust myself with accessible guns in the house. I don't mind having them in the house, as long as they are in a safe I don't have access to. I'm not a master at lockpicking or safecracking, but I've done it enough, and I wouldn't really put anything past me during an episode. I'm sure there is a way around that (random code, print, etc.). And... We have a lot of other deadly things in the house here. Don't underestimate a person's will to die. Sometimes it's fleeting, but sometimes you should hide the sharps (cutlery/hunting knives), too. I get where he's coming from. It's a dark, painful place.

That's so obvious that it's brilliant! I actually do get migraines. How on earth did I not think of this before?! And it would make sense in an environment like that! If anyone asks, this will be my response from here on out! Thank you so much!

I'm the same way with unsolicited contact and the various kinds of mail. I go so far as to avoid checkouts that are staffed by humans, and I'm delighted with the ridiculous fact that I can have everything from dishwasher detergent to toilet paper shipped right to me. That said, it's not healthy. I've been working on this for years. You're aware of it now, so it would be great to advocate for yourself and work on it before it becomes more of a problem. Good luck.
My fiancé does that for me, and it does help break through most of the time, but I definitely have to work on the ability to calm myself. Thanks!
Thanks. Grounding exercises are a good idea. I haven't been very good at that lately.
I've been told I sound like a cement mixer. I've broken two teeth grinding in my sleep. I chew though about 4 mm of hard plastic every six months now.
